Example Input and Expected Output:
Input:

Expected Output:

  • Summary statistics of transactions per category.

  • Identification of outliers and anomalies in transaction amounts.
  • Predictive model forecasting future spending patterns.

Python Code:

# advanced_data_analysis_and_statistical_modeling_with_pandas.py

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from statsmodels.tsa.arima.model import ARIMA

# Load dataset
data: pd.DataFrame = pd.read_csv('financial_transactions.csv')

# Data preprocessing
data['Date'] = pd.to_datetime(data['Date'])
data.sort_values('Date', inplace=True)
data.dropna(inplace=True)

# Feature engineering
data['Month'] = data['Date'].dt.month
data['Year'] = data['Date'].dt.year
data['DayOfWeek'] = data['Date'].dt.dayofweek

# Summary statistics
summary: pd.DataFrame = data.groupby('Category')['Amount'].describe()

# Visualization
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.lineplot(x='Date', y='Amount', data=data)
plt.title('Spending Over Time')
plt.xlabel('Date')
plt.ylabel('Amount')
plt.show()

# Outlier detection
q1: float = data['Amount'].quantile(0.25)
q3: float = data['Amount'].quantile(0.75)
iqr: float = q3 - q1
outliers: pd.DataFrame = data[(data['Amount'] < (q1 - 1.5 * iqr)) | (data['Amount'] > (q3 + 1.5 * iqr))]

# Predictive modeling
features: pd.DataFrame = data[['Amount', 'Month', 'DayOfWeek']]
target: pd.Series = data['Amount']
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(features, target, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)
model: LinearRegression = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
predictions: np.ndarray = model.predict(X_test)

# Time series forecasting
data.set_index('Date', inplace=True)
monthly_data: pd.Series = data['Amount'].resample('M').sum()
arima_model = ARIMA(monthly_data, order=(1, 1, 1))
arima_result = arima_model.fit()
forecast: pd.Series = arima_result.forecast(steps=12)

# Plot forecast
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
monthly_data.plot(label='Historical')
forecast.plot(label='Forecast', linestyle='--')
plt.title('Monthly Spending Forecast')
plt.xlabel('Date')
plt.ylabel('Amount')
plt.legend()
plt.show()
